entries.mechanism: TAXSIM runs at its latest 2024 law year. For the single 30,000-dollar filer both years apply the same 2.75 per cent rate to Ohio taxable income (27,600) above the 26,050 no-tax threshold and the same 20-dollar exemption credit (taxable income below 30,000), so the entire 28.69-dollar gap is the section 5747.02(A)(3) base-amount indexation: 360.69 at the 2024 first-bracket effective rate of 1.38462 per cent versus 332.00 at the 2026 rate of 1.27448 per cent. The pipeline reports 354.63 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 383.32. This is a pinned-2024-law-year vintage, not a pipeline defect; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.

For the single 60,000-dollar filer (taxable income 57,850, entirely below the 100,000-dollar threshold) both years apply the same 2.75 per cent rate above 26,050, so the 28.70-dollar gap is the section 5747.02(A)(3) base-amount indexation (360.69 in 2024 versus 332.00 in 2026). The 2024 schedule 360.69 + 0.0275*(57850-26050) = 1235.19 reproduces TAXSIM's 1235.20 to the cent; the pipeline reports 1206.50. Pinned-2024-law-year vintage; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.

For the single 150,000-dollar filer two 2024-to-2026 vintage changes drive the 455.94-dollar residual: the section 5747.02(A)(3) base amount (360.69 in 2024 versus 332.00 in 2026) and Ohio's 2024 law taxing Ohio taxable income above 100,000 at a 3.5 per cent top marginal rate that House Bill 33 collapsed into the single 2.75 per cent rate by 2026. The 2024 schedule 360.69 + 0.0275*(100000-26050) + 0.035*(150000-100000) = 4144.315 reproduces TAXSIM's 4144.32 to the cent; the pipeline reports 3688.38. Pinned-2024-law-year vintage; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.

For the married 60,000-dollar filer (taxable income 55,700, below the 100,000-dollar threshold) both years apply the same 2.75 per cent rate above 26,050, so the 28.69-dollar gap is the section 5747.02(A)(3) base-amount indexation (360.69 in 2024 versus 332.00 in 2026). The 2024 schedule 360.69 + 0.0275*(55700-26050) = 1176.07 reproduces TAXSIM's 1176.07 to the cent; the pipeline reports 1147.38. Pinned-2024-law-year vintage; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.

For the married 120,000-dollar filer two 2024-to-2026 vintage changes drive the 283.19-dollar residual: the section 5747.02(A)(3) base amount (360.69 in 2024 versus 332.00 in 2026) and the 2024 law's 3.5 per cent top marginal rate on Ohio taxable income above 100,000 that House Bill 33 collapsed into the single 2.75 per cent rate by 2026. The 2024 schedule 360.69 + 0.0275*(100000-26050) + 0.035*(120000-100000) = 3094.315 reproduces TAXSIM's 3094.32 to the cent; the pipeline reports 2811.13. Pinned-2024-law-year vintage; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.

For the married 300,000-dollar filer two 2024-to-2026 vintage changes drive the 1633.19-dollar residual: the section 5747.02(A)(3) base amount (360.69 in 2024 versus 332.00 in 2026) and the 2024 law's 3.5 per cent top marginal rate on Ohio taxable income above 100,000 that House Bill 33 collapsed into the single 2.75 per cent rate by 2026. The 2024 schedule 360.69 + 0.0275*(100000-26050) + 0.035*(300000-100000) = 9394.315 reproduces TAXSIM's 9394.32 to the cent; the pipeline reports 7761.13. Pinned-2024-law-year vintage; the pipeline matches PolicyEngine at 2026 to the cent.
